correctness.rationale: The shear matrix in RESULT.md:24–37 is the a.e. differential in orthonormal polar frames up to a rotation. The regularity step holds even at the origin: for |z|=r≥s=|w|>0, splitting off the change of rotation gives |T(z)−T(w)|≤|z−w|+Ss log(r/s)≤(1+S)|z−w|; the same argument applies to the inverse and the zero-radius case is immediate. Thus the a.e. singular-value ratio of the determinant-one shear gives the exact maximal dilatation, with log K=2 asinh(S/2). In curvature −1, putting u=log(1/r)>0 in the exact equal-radius distance formula gives sinh(d/2)=|sin(φ(r)/2)|/sinh u≤Su/(2 sinh u)≤S/2 by absolute continuity and φ(1)=0. For φ(r)=c log r the ratio tends to c/2 at the boundary, including the trivial c=0 case. For positive S the bound is strict at each interior point, so the finding correctly asserts equality of suprema rather than interior attainment. The bundled checker and its recorded output only sample scalar identities and boundary approach; no fresh execution or formal verification is claimed.
residual_risks: No extension to general boundary-fixing quasiconformal disk maps is proved.

value.rationale: The displacement is the same invariant used to characterize the identity-boundary preservation kernel and is central to the classical disk distortion problem. For each specified K the result gives the exact optimum over all admissible radial angular profiles, not merely the distortion of a familiar spiral. It provides a sharp benchmark, approached at the boundary, without claiming improvement for the unrestricted class.
residual_risks: This is a subclass result and does not change the optimal unrestricted disk bound.
